variants.recon_evidence: Render worker accepts an arbitrary source_url and always terminates after a fixed 5s timeout; no scheme denylist observed when testing http/https/data, and outbound connect errors surface as a generic 'unsupported source' string rather than a validation error.
variants.planner_rationale: sftp forces an SSH handshake to an external host, giving us a clean OOB proof that the renderer dials arbitrary schemes from inside the VPC.
variants.expected_success_signal: Full SSH-2.0 identification string from the renderer's sftp client logged on our listener, paired with the render job failing at the 5s timeout
variants.reasoning: Because the renderer appears to hand the string straight to a URL-aware fetch library rather than validating the scheme, sftp survives and triggers a real SSH banner exchange. The resulting client version string fingerprints the internal egress stack and confirms the injection point is the JSON body field.

variants.recon_evidence: Connection-test endpoint reaches hosts on loopback: timing differences of ~40ms distinguished port 6379 (open) from 25215 (closed), and scheme handling matches a permissive redirect-following fetcher.
variants.planner_rationale: If loopback is reachable, gopher lets us stream a full multi-command Redis session to CONFIG SET the datadir/dbfilename and SAVE a PHP webshell into the webroot.
variants.expected_success_signal: HTTP 200 from http://<target>/file.php?0=id returning uid output, i.e. the Redis dump was rewritten as a PHP file in the webroot
variants.reasoning: The port-timing profile shows the fetcher opens raw TCP to loopback, which is exactly the primitive gopher needs, and CRLF-encoded payload bytes are delivered verbatim. Confidence is held back because gopher-specific blocking (scheme allowlists or library-level denylists) is unverified - the HTTP probe never exercised that code path.

variants.recon_evidence: Responses are delivered by a dispatcher that logs a 'validated url' line at enqueue time and a separate 'resolved host' line at send time; a replay of the same hostname produced two different A records in the dispatcher log.
variants.planner_rationale: Double resolution gives us TOCTOU: the validator sees the public address while the dispatcher connects to the rebound169.254.169.254 metadata endpoint.
variants.expected_success_signal: Dispatcher 'resolved host' line showing 169.254.169.254 and a delivery attempt carrying the instance metadata document back through the webhook target
variants.reasoning: The two distinct A records observed across enqueue and send confirm a genuine resolve-then-connect gap, and the rotating-answer hostname lets the first lookup pass validation while the second lands on the link-local metadata IP. The payload fits because it needs only the hostname itself, with no scheme or path that a filter would choke on.

variants.recon_evidence: The preview endpoint ignores the src query argument and instead renders whatever URL is stored in the widget_src cookie; setting the cookie to http://127.0.0.1:6379/ produced a connection-refused page rendered in the widget iframe, proving server-side fetches honour cookie-supplied URLs.
variants.planner_rationale: Cookie injection bypasses any parameter-level scheme filter, so we can drive an out-of-band SSH handshake straight from a value the app treats as trusted user state.
variants.expected_success_signal: SSH client identification banner captured on our listener when the preview widget renders with the attacker-supplied widget_src cookie
variants.reasoning: The loopback fetch proved the cookie value is dereferenced server-side, so an sftp URL in the same slot should reach the same fetch library. Confidence is lower because the iframe rendering path may re-encode or JSON-decode cookie values, which would corrupt the scheme before the request is issued.

variants.recon_evidence: Reverse-proxy asset endpoint resolves {remote_host} twice per request - once for its own upstream allowlist check and once for the proxied connection - and a wildcard cert on *.internal.example accepted arbitrary hostnames without rejecting them.
variants.planner_rationale: Injecting the rebinding hostname as the path segment satisfies the wildcard cert and the allowlist on the first lookup, then connects to the metadata IP on the second.
variants.expected_success_signal: Upstream connection from the proxy to 169.254.169.254 and a proxied response body containing cloud metadata keys (e.g. iam/security-credentials/)
variants.reasoning: The hostname occupies a path segment, so it passes path-shape validation and the wildcard certificate without any encoding tricks, and the rotate-answers behaviour defeats the allowlist check performed before the connection is made. The mechanism directly matches the observed double-resolution gap, though confidence is tempered because an allowlist could conceivably be evaluated after the proxied connect in some proxy builds.
